base: Hu. = ACLT 2 docs/96 ("KARATEPE 1 Hu."); Ho. = ACLT 2 docs/176 ("KARATEPE 1 Ho."), both parsed from saved pages (.github/pipeline/run3/probe/aclt-doc96.html, aclt-doc176.html)

field_guide.translit: ACLT sign-by-sign transliteration of the written word, markup kept: {X}=italic capitals (syllabic sign inside a ligature/compound), ^I=superscript personal-name marker, ^?/^!=superscript query/sic, subscripts as Unicode ₂₃₄₅ₓ; | word divider, || register (line) break, ˹ ˺ partly damaged, [ ] lost/restored, < > editorial supplement, << >> erased/superfluous signs, “ ” logogram quotation marks, <“> <”> bracketed quotation mark.
field_guide.lb_before: register break (||) immediately before this written word -> pilot word.nl
field_guide.signs[].lb_before: register break inside the word, before this sign -> pilot glyph.nl
field_guide.signs[].unit: pilot-style glyph unit: signs joined by + (ligature, e.g. wa/i+ra/i, AEDIFICARE+MI) or . (compound, e.g. OMNIS.MI, BOS.ANIMA) share one unit = one pilot glyph
field_guide.signs[].role_hint: det = in parentheses (or ^I); log = capitals; phon = lower case or italic capitals. phon vs comp (phonetic complement) is the drafter's call — ACLT does not mark it.
field_guide.signs[].sign / sign_source: Laroche key (A###) and where it comes from: pilot (already used in the shipped pilot), laroche (ACLT gives L###), memory (unverified candidate — check before use), unknown (no candidate), none (not a sign).
field_guide.signs[].damage: partial (˹ ˺), lost ([ ]), mixed (bracket opens/closes inside the sign label; see damage_detail)
field_guide.signs[].quoted: logogram inside “ ” (Unicode has A410 BEGIN LOGOGRAM MARK / A410A END LOGOGRAM MARK; the pilot dropped them)
field_guide.transcription: ACLT interpreted word for the whole written word
field_guide.transcription_words: ACLT transcription layer split into clitic pieces: text, lemma, pos, pos_sub, gloss (ACLT trans_en), gr (ACLT grammatical features); kind=joiner is the = between clitics
field_guide.parallel: the Ho. text of the same clause, reference only
